note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. The patient reports that he was doing some yard work in the last week or so and started to feel really tired and short of breath. He believes that he caught his first cold in the last few weeks and that it has gotten worse. The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression, but he is concerned about this episode of illness. He has been attending barre classes to help him relax. The patient reports that he has been monitoring his blood sugar levels while at work during the week, but not on weekends. He notes that his diet has been good for the most part, except for house parties and things like that. His blood pressure has been under control with home monitoring, but not on weekends.

The patient denies fevers, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or muscle aches or joint pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Respiratory: Shortness of breath.
• Musculoskeletal: Joint pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Strongly regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops or rubs.
Respiratory: Scattered ronchi bilaterally on auscultation of lungs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray obtained today shows no airspace disease or pneumonia.
Hemoglobin A1c 8.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. I believe this to be viral syndrome based on his symptoms and examination findings today. We will send a COVID test to rule out COVID-19 exposure. I have recommended Robitussin for cough and ibuprofen/tylenol for fever management.

For his depression, we discussed this further today and I have recommended referral to psychotherapy if he would like to pursue this option at a later date.

For his type 2 diabetes, I have recommended increasing metformin to 1000 mg twice daily and we will follow up in 4 months with another hemoglobin A1c.

For his hypertension, we discussed this further today and I have recommended continuing lisinopril 20 mg daily. We will order a lipid panel as well as refill lisinopril.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrea Roberts is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux who presents today for her annual exam. She has been doing well. She has been walking and exercising and doing yoga, which has helped with her arthritis. She has not had any joint pain recently. She is still taking methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly without any issues. She has been experiencing palpitations, which she notes started about a week ago when she was stressed. She has tried meditation and running with her dog to relieve stress but it hasn't helped. Her last event monitor showed that she is in and out of atrial fibrillation with a conversion pause.

Regarding her reflux, she has been cutting out soda and that seemed to help. The protonix 40 mg daily has also helped and she hasn't had a flare up in over five months.

She endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports well.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain to palpation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm at this time.
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Autoimmune panel: Normal.
• Event monitor: Positive for conversion pause.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Rheumatoid arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: Everything looks good on autoimmune panel today. We have continued the methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly as tolerated.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed the importance of adhering to the methotrexate regimen as prescribed by the rheumatologist.
- Medical Treatment: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly as tolerated until next visit.
- Referral: If needed, we will refer back to the rheumatologist for further evaluation.
- Patient Agreements/Informed Consent: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan today.
• Atrial fibrillation.
- Medical Reasoning: You are going in and out of atrial fibrillation with a conversion pause on your event monitor today. We discussed this today in detail as well as the benefits of performing a cardiac ablation to map out where your rhythm is coming from and burn it so it doesn't come back again in the future given your age and history of atrial fibrillation going in and out of sinus rhythm multiple times per day.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed the benefits of performing a cardiac ablation today as well as what to expect from this procedure including recovery time, complications, etc., prior to proceeding with this procedure today.
- Medical Treatment: Order referral to cardiology for cardiac ablation today.
- Patient Agreements/Informed Consent: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan today.
• Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
- Medical Reasoning: Everything looks good on autoimmune panel today. We have continued protonix 40 mg daily as tolerated until next visit due to improvement in symptoms since starting protonix 40 mg daily last month along with dietary modifications including avoiding coffee and spicy foods, etc., which have also helped improve symptoms since starting these modifications last month.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications including avoiding coffee, spicy foods, etc., which have also helped improve symptoms since starting these modifications last month along with lifestyle modifications such as weight loss if needed or smoking cessation if applicable prior to proceeding with these recommendations today.
- Medical Treatment: Continue protonix 40 mg daily until next visit along with dietary modifications including avoiding coffee, spicy foods, etc., which have also helped improve symptoms since starting these modifications last month prior to proceeding with these recommendations today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Emergency room follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male who presents today for emergency room follow-up. The patient reports that he was not staying on top of his blood sugar readings and felt woozy over the weekend. He was concerned and his wife wanted to take him in for evaluation. The patient reports that his blood sugar was elevated at that time. He denies being admitted to the hospital, but was seen by a physician who recommended dietary modifications.

The patient reports that he has been doing well since returning home from the visit. He notes that he has been eating more consistently during the week, but still eats out frequently on the weekends. The patient notes that he has been doing well with his kidney transplant medications and is following doctor’s orders.

Regarding his depression, the patient reports that it has been a tough year-and-a-half, but he has been doing well with it as long as he finds time to relax in the afternoon.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Respiratory: Denies lightheadedness or dizziness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: No carotid bruits heard.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: 8.
Fasting Glucose: 162.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male who presents today for emergency room follow-up. His current medical problems include depression, type 2 diabetes, and kidney transplant.
• Hyperglycemia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s hemoglobin A1c is elevated at this time and his fasting glucose was elevated at the time of his emergency room visit. We discussed dietary modifications with him today and I recommended increasing his lantus dose to 20 units at night. We will recheck his hemoglobin A1c in 2 months.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: I advised him to continue monitoring his blood sugar levels and we will adjust further if needed.
• Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well with meditation as a coping mechanism for stress management. We discussed holding off on medical therapy at this time and we will continue to monitor him closely for any additional symptoms or signs of depression.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed continued use of meditation as an effective coping mechanism for stress management until we can discuss additional options in detail later this week.
• Kidney transplant.
- Medical Reasoning: His kidney function appears stable at this time. We discussed continuing immunosuppression medications as prescribed by Dr. Reyes and recommended contacting me if there are any concerns regarding these medications or if additional support is needed moving forward.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: I advised him to contact me if there are any concerns regarding these medications or if additional support is needed moving forward.

He notes that he has been experiencing lack of sleep, which has been getting to him. He has tried melatonin, meditation, and t- stretching out every morning when he gets up, but nothing seems to help.

Regarding his multiple sclerosis, the patient last saw the neurologist 6 months ago. He is currently taking his medication and reports no additional weakness.

Amanda Martinez is a 43-year-old female who presents today for right arm pain. The onset of her symptoms began after she was playing tennis and hit the top of the net with her arm. She denies any swelling or numbness in her hand. She does report some pain when moving her wrist.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right arm pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness in her hand.

Musculoskeletal: Tenderness over distal radius on exam.

RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is a 43-year-old female who presents today for right arm pain. She reports that she hit the top of the net with her arm while playing tennis and denies any swelling or numbness in her hand. She does report some pain when moving her wrist.

The patient's exam is significant for tenderness over distal radius on exam.
X-rays were reviewed today by Dr. Gomez and there are no fractures or abnormalities noted.
I have discussed conservative treatment options with the patient today, including ice, anti-inflammatory, and Motrin 800 mg three times a day with food. We will follow up if symptoms do not improve in 1 week.

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Cheryl Ramirez is a 34-year-old female who presents today with back pain. The onset of her back pain began approximately 6 days ago after she had been walking for 30 minutes to an hour. She denies any trauma prior to the onset of her back pain. She endorses that she has been lifting more weight around 3 times a week, and she suspects that this may have contributed to her back pain. She denies any numbness, tingling, or weakness in her lower extremities. She endorses nasal congestion from seasonal allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Endorses back pain.
• Neurological: Denies numbness, tingling, or weakness in lower extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border. Otherwise, no murmurs or gallops.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the spine reveals tenderness to palpation on the right lateral aspect of the lumbar spine with pain with flexion and extension.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Back x-ray obtained today was reviewed by me in office today. There is good bony alignment without evidence of fracture.
Labs were reviewed today and are all within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Lumbar strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with new onset back pain without any history of trauma. She endorses right-sided tenderness to palpation on the lumbar spine with pain with flexion and extension as well as a negative straight leg raise test.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient that this is likely due to a lumbar strain secondary to lifting or exercising and recommended ice and heat application as well as physical therapy for strengthening exercises of her back.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management. We will follow up in clinic in 2 weeks if symptoms do not improve.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure has been well controlled at home since we last saw her in clinic last month when we discussed lifestyle modifications including diet changes and weight loss strategies such as weight training with her partner.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including diet changes and weight loss strategies such as weight training with her partner again today at clinic today.
- Medical Treatment: We will continue lisinopril 10 mg daily as prescribed.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Colds.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Randy Gutierrez is a 9-month-old male who presents today for evaluation of a cold.

The patient started to develop a runny nose and congestion last night. He also has been pulling on his ears and rubbing at his nose. His mother notes that his mucous is clear. He has been drooling and has been irritable. His appetite has been decreased, but he did eat some cereal this morning. He is still fighting to sleep.

His mother notes that the patient's older sister has been sick as well as their play date with the patient's nephew who had a sinus infection.

The patient's mother reports that she has tried saline mist in his nose, Tylenol, and baby Vick's on his feet last night to try and help him breathe. She also used the humidifier.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fever.
• Respiratory: Cough, runny nose, congestion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Ears: No discharge or erythema.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Today the patient presents for evaluation of a cold.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient appears to be experiencing a viral upper respiratory infection. Often sinus infections will start out as a virus and then will become bacterial infections if left alone and does not go away. However, I do not think he needs any antibiotics at this point in time.
• Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options today including saline mist in his nose, Tylenol for fever control, baby Vick's on his feet last night to try and help him breathe, and using the humidifier. We also discussed that we would watch him very carefully for a barking cough. If he does develop one we would give him half a teaspoon of his sister’s medicine daily for 5 days until it resolves. We discussed that we would continue to monitor him closely for worsening symptoms or signs of worsening illness such as fever greater than 100 degrees Fahrenheit or increased irritability or lethargy.
• Patient Education: I advised the parents that they should continue to keep up with fluids, rest, and watch him very carefully for a barking cough. If he develops one they should give him half a teaspoon of his sister’s medicine daily for 5 days until it resolves. They should avoid honey until after their first birthday due to botulism spores being present in honey which can cause harm to infants under 1 year old.
• Additional Testing: No additional testing was recommended today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acne.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of acne. The onset of acne began approximately 2 years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which is somewhat helpful. There are no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: No additional past medical history.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives with parents and sister. They have a dog, bird, and rabbits in the home. She is in 7th grade and active in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing.

FAMILY HISTORY

No significant family medical history.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Skin: Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities. Scattered skin colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythmateous papules on the face, primarily on the forehead and with also some on the central cheeks and chin. The chest and back are relatively spared.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of acne.
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comodonal with small inflammatory component.
- Medical Reasoning: Mild to moderate acne was noted on exam today.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options today including topical therapy first. Every morning she will wash her face with a mild cleanser then use a moisturizer labeled "noncomedogenic," with sunscreen SPF 30 or higher. This means it won't clog her pores. Now in the evening wash her face with the same cleanser and allow it to dry. Apply adapalene 0.1% cream in a thin layer to areas where she generally gets acne. I want her to start off using this a few nights a week and slowly work up to using it every night if it is very expensive or not covered by insurance you can try different gel over-the-counter products such as Clean & Clear Persa-Gel in a thin layer or where she generally gets acne followed by noncomedogenic moisturizer.
- Patient Education: We discussed atopic retinoid will cause some sensitivity so she will need to wear sunscreen when outside this may also cause some dryness or irritation.

Breast reduction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments, but the minimal relief. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing back pain since high school. She has been going to the chiropractor for a few years and notes that she does have bra strap indentations in her shoulders. She also notes that she experiences numbness and tingling in her hands and nipple pain. She also reports that she is currently studying psychology.

The patient denies any history of breast cancer in her family. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use drugs.

She reports that she has been experiencing sweating underneath her breasts and feels limited by the size of her breasts when working out or running/jumping.

She denies any history of mammograms. Her mother was 40 years old when she had breast cancer.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports weight loss over the past few months.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports back pain, neck pain, and shoulder pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Breast: Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments, but the minimal relief. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

The physical exam findings of the breasts reveal asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. There is no nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy is palpable.

Patient Agreements Obtained: Patient understands and agrees with recommended surgical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Renal ultrasound.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kelly Wood is a 41-year-old female who presents today for a renal ultrasound because of hematuria. She reports that she passed two stones last week and has had several episodes of bright red urine the color of cherry kool-aid. She also reports that she has been constantly having to urinate and it has been painful. Her pain was rated at an 8 on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being no pain and 10 being the worst pain imaginable. She denies any flank pain or tenderness in her lower back.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Urinary: Hematuria.
• Genitourinary: Pain.
• Constitutional: Fever.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Abdomen: No flank pain.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Urine dipstick today. Negative for leukocytes, nitrates, protein, ketone, bilirubin and glucose. Color yellow and clear, urobilinogen 0.2, pH 5.5 and specific gravity 1.020. There is a trace amount of blood in the urine and intact.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ms. Wood is an established patient here for renal ultrasound because of hematuria.
Primary diagnosis: Hematuria.
Secondary diagnosis: Chronic urolithiasis.
Medical Reasoning: The patient's hematuria was due to kidney stones as evidenced by the trace amount of blood in her urine today on urinalysis as well as her history of passing stones last week. Fortunately, she passed two stones last week and the blood has nearly subsided.
Plan: I discussed with the patient that since her kidney stone is not obstructing or causing pain at this time, we do not recommend any surgical intervention at this time. We discussed dietary recommendations to help prevent future stone formation including drinking half her body weight in ounces of water a day and avoiding sugary drinks like Mountain Dew as well as reducing sodium intake to less than 1,000 mg per day and reducing animal protein consumption such as beef, poultry, fish and pork.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Sanchez is a 58-year-old female who presents today for status post mitral valve repair done on 8/3/2020. She reports that she was having a rough time before surgery, but she feels much better now. She denies any new symptoms at this visit. She does experience chest pain, but it only lasts for a few minutes and then resolves for a while. She notes that it happens often enough for her to notice. She has been trying to keep up with her medications, but she has been using a reminder app to help her remember them.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
Respiratory: Reports shallow breathing.
note.objective_exam:

Head and Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Respiratory: Reduced breath sounds bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular rhythm.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

ECG taken on 12/26/2020 reveals atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly. Compared to the previous study, there are no significant changes.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is doing well from a cardiac standpoint and we recommended she continue with the same medication regimen as previously discussed today. We reviewed her ECG from 12/26/2020 which revealed atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response and t-wave inversion anteriorly compared to the previous study, there are no significant changes.

Patient Agreements.
I have discussed the medical treatment plan outlined above in detail with the patient and have obtained verbal consent.

New worrisome heart murmur.

She also reports lightheadedness and dizziness, which she treats with meclizine. She denies fevers, chills, irregular heartbeats, or passing out.

She notes that her symptoms have improved from 70-80% since last month. Her symptoms were completely absent prior to last month.

She denies any history of smoking and no known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY

The patient reports that her son had a myocardial infarction. Her brother had a stroke and is diabetic. Her older sister has an unknown heart problem. Heart disease runs in the family.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she requires a walker to ambulate.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Endorses dyspnea on exertion.
Neurological: Endorses lightheadedness and dizziness.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diana Scott is a 100-year-old female who presents today for a new patient evaluation.
Probable one cardiac murmur.
Diana has a 4/6 systolic murmur at the upper right sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids. This is most likely representative of aortic stenosis, for symptoms could be due to severe aortic stenosis. However, her S2 is relatively preserved, which would be more consistent with moderate. Some of her outside records do note diastolic dysfunction, so it is possible she did have an echocardiogram at some point in the past. She does not appear significantly volume overloaded today.
Her next problem is PVCs. Her referral mentioned tachycardia. Her EKG today shows sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs, as well as an anterior septum infarct pattern. She does not have any significant palpitations and we will check an echocardiogram to assess overall cardiac structure and function depending on results as well as the severity of her aortic stenosis, we will need to consider an ischemic evaluation or further possibly a heart monitor to assess overall burden of the PVCs. At this point she's asymptomatic so we will start with the echocardiogram only.
Her next problem hypolipidemia is managed by her PCP.
Due to bilateral leg pain over the last month considered TAVR evaluation following echocardiogram.
Statin could be indicated due to bilateral leg pain over the last month.
Her next problem lightheadedness/dizziness treated with meclizine for this reason it is possible that some of her lightheadedness and dizziness are related to the Aortic Stenosis we will do an echocardiogram as noted above PVCs on her EKG could be contributing but she does not feel palpitations we will consider monitor but start with echocardiogram first as noted above follow up three to four weeks after her echocardiogram done to discuss results and next steps.

We will schedule allergy testing next week.

Back pain.

Bryan Brooks is a 39-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of back pain. The onset of his symptoms began yesterday when he was raking leaves in his yard. He denies any prior history of back pain, but reports that he had experienced this once about 3 years ago which resolved after a day. He has tried icing and Advil for the pain, but these did not help. The patient states that his symptoms are better when he is laying down or sitting, but hurts more when standing up. He notes that his partner also experiences back pain when standing up.

The patient denies any prior physical activity, but reports that his partner has been doing a lot of yard work lately.

Neurological: Reports right leg tingling.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the low back were obtained today and reviewed by me in office today. There were no abnormalities noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Bryan Brooks is a 39-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of low back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with a lumbar sprain.

- Patient Education: I have explained to him that we will follow up in 2 weeks if there is no improvement in symptoms and we may consider an MRI if needed at that time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gregory Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that he has had the ulcer for approximately 2 months and it has recently become red and is draining. He was concerned about how it has healed. The patient states that he believes he may have gotten the ulcer from walking barefoot on the beach. He did see his primary care provider before coming in today, but they did not prescribe antibiotics for him. He does not recall the name of the medication prescribed, but he believes it was something he had taken before. The patient also reports that he was at Dewey Beach in his ambulance when he got the ulcer.

The patient denies any specific pain, but does report some throbbing. He notes that this is his first time experiencing drainage with an ulcer.

The patient reports that his diabetes is well controlled with medication, but does not check his sugars regularly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Skin: Reports erythema and drainage of right foot ulcer.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Skin: There is a 1x2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the 5th metatarsophalangeal joint. There is some erythema and drainage present. There is edema around it. There is fluid like you said that's coming out of it. I do not see any necrosis, odor or bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot reveals no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Gregory Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.
• Medical Reasoning: This appears to be a diabetic foot ulcer secondary to poor glycemic control.
• Medical Treatment: We will order an ABI ankle brachial index just to determine blood supply in his foot to see if we can actually heal this ulcer today. We will also perform debridement to remove dead tissue and prescribe clindamycin 400 mg twice daily for 7 days to try to get rid of this infection which you currently do have and that will get rid of some of that redness and drainage that's happening now.
• Patient Education: I discussed with him today that if anything happens between now and our next visit we should call us at (insert office number) so we can get him in immediately if there are any issues or if it's an emergency if he feels like he's getting a fever or feeling ill, please go to urgent care or ER if he feels like getting black or anything like that but otherwise we'll see him back in 2 weeks.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Right foot wound.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Wayne Jenkins is a 43-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for a sore on his right foot that is not healing. The patient purchased a new pair of shoes to travel with and the neuropathy he has been experiencing did not feel that they were too tight at first. He initially had a blister, but it soon became a wound and he was seen by his PCP. He was placed on antibiotics, which he completed yesterday. The wound looks about the same now. He denies any changes to the appearance of the wound, pain or drainage. Occasionally, he has issues with stability, which was a primary purpose of purchasing these shoes. He denies fever or chills.

The patient reports neuropathy.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports instability.
• Skin: Reports wound on right foot that is not healing.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Skin: There is a 1 by 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the right fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. There is some yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection. There is no necrosis present and there is no odor present. I do not appreciate any bony exposure on vascular exam. Palpable bilateral femoral and popliteal pulses are present but no palpable DP or PT pulses are present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of right foot today shows no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right diabetic foot ulcer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for a sore on his right foot that is not healing. His last hemoglobin A1C was 8%. We reviewed his x-ray today which showed no evidence of osteomyelitis which means there is no evidence of bone infection.
• Medical Treatment: I have reviewed the results today and discussed them with him in detail in regards to his diabetic foot ulcer today. We discussed options for treatment including debridement in office, collagenase ointment application once daily, dry sterile dressing coverage, surgical shoe wear to take pressure off area until we see improvement in wound size and pink tissue formation.
• Patient Education: We discussed importance of keeping diabetes under control in order to heal this ulcer.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Recent blood work.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Walker is a 68-year-old female who presents today for recent blood work. She reports that her primary care provider recently ordered blood work and informed her that she has hepatitis C. She is surprised because she has been feeling fine. She denies any history of intravenous drug use, but admits to partying a lot and using IV drugs years ago. She currently smokes 1-2 cigarettes per day, previously 1 to 1.5 packs per day, and drinks approximately 1 beer per day, more on the weekends. She denies any known hepatitis C positive partners.

She reports that she used to drink a lot of alcohol, but now drinks about 1 beer per day. She used to smoke up to one pack and a half per day, but has cut down to 1-2 cigarettes per day.

She denies any other medication conditions.

The patient reports that she had her physical there was nothing else the only thing she was telling her PCP is that she does feel like she tends to be really tired at the end of the day after working but otherwise she's been good.

She notes that work has been busy lately but not much more than usual.

The patient notes that she tends to be a workaholic but is working on it.

Her family history is significant for hypertension, diabetes, and depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General: Appears in no distress. No jaundice on skin exam.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with a 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

HCV antibody: Positive.
AST: 39; Within normal limits.
ALT: Within normal limits.
Albumin: Within normal limits.
Bilirubin, total: Within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Jacqueline Walker is a 68-year-old female who presents today for recent blood work. Her HCV antibody test was positive and her liver panel showed an elevated AST at 39; however, her ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin were all within normal limits. This all means that her initial labs are consistent with hepatitis C. Based on the discussion I just had with you today there now hepatitis C is a viral infection that affects the liver so you most likely may have had it for years now so the next step that I would like to do is to confirm the diagnosis with some additional blood work that includes checking the HCV RNA and also the HCV genotype. We will also determine the severity of your liver disease by checking for fibrosis of the liver which we will do by ordering a special ultrasound with this information I will be able to know how to proceed as far as treatment.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Jenkins is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of headaches. She has been experiencing headaches since she was a teenager and they used to be around her menstrual periods but as she got older she noticed that they were with that and also when she is really stressed. Recently, her headaches have been getting a lot more frequent and severe. She has noticed that they seem to get worse around her menstrual periods but also when she is exercising. She has been trying to exercise more in order to lose weight but can't even really exercise for very long because her headaches come back on a lot worse. She has been experiencing ringing in her ears for a few months now and then what really scared her was that now she's starting to get some blurred vision on the side of her vision. She denies any numbness or tingling to her hands or feet or face.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Headache: Yes.
• Ear: Yes.
• Vision: Yes.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
- Cranial nerves 1-12 are intact including normal cranial reflexes.
- Gait is normal.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for the evaluation of headaches. Her symptoms are concerning for idiopathic intracranial hypertension, which is increased pressure in the brain without any known cause. This can present with symptoms such as worsening with activity, ringing in the ears, changes in vision, etc. We discussed this today and I have referred her for an MRI of the brain today as well as a spinal tap to help evaluate the pressure in the brain and possibly decrease it by taking fluid off of it. We will also be seeing a neuro-ophthalmologist for a complete eye exam today.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

The patient presents today for evaluation of neck strain secondary to motor vehicle accident.

The patient understands and agrees with my recommended medical treatment plan.

note.assessment_and_plan:

For your first problem, the left shoulder pain, your symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy. I also want to refer you to physical therapy for approximately 6-8 weeks and continue Tylenol during this time. William Smith is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began 3 weeks ago after he started playing tennis more frequently. He denies any trauma to the right elbow. The patient reports that the pain is localized to the lateral aspect of his right elbow and is described as sharp, shooting, and throbbing. The pain is worse with movement and better with rest. He has tried taking Tylenol and ibuprofen but they do not help with his symptoms. He has also tried icing his right elbow but it does not seem to help.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the right arm or hand.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 3 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border, unchanged from prior exam.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right elbow reveals moderate lateral epicondylar tenderness. Pain with passive range of motion of the right elbow, no palpable joint effusion, mild pain with resisted extension of the right wrist.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow today shows no acute fracture or other bony abnormality. There is no malalignment or sign of joint effusion.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute lateral epicondylitis of the right elbow.
- Medical Reasoning: This is likely due to overuse secondary to increased tennis activity.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I explained that this is also known as tennis elbow and recommended that he rest his arm as much as possible for 4-6 weeks while avoiding repetitive stress in that arm. I advised him to ice his right elbow for 20 minutes at least 3 times per day and recommended that he use a brace for his forearm to help reduce discomfort.
- Medical Treatment: I prescribed Ultram 50 mg once daily for pain management.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with these recommendations.

2. Diabetes type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood sugars are a bit elevated due to eating too many Cadbury eggs during Easter weekend.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed how we need to make some adjustments in order to get his blood sugars under control including increasing his metformin dosage from 500 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily, checking his blood sugar twice daily for the next two weeks, and ordering additional labs including a hemoglobin A1c level and CBC blood test today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Asthma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Lewis is a 66-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for worsening asthma symptoms. The patient reports that she has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the past 6 months. She notes that her symptoms tend to worsen when she gets sick with a cold and that she has had several exacerbations in the past year. She also notes that she has had several visits to urgent care and her primary care provider due to her asthma symptoms. She reports that she has been prescribed prednisone in the past, but does not remember the exact dose or duration of treatment. The patient denies any history of smoking or vaping.

The patient reports that she enjoys hiking and going outside, but notes that she avoids going to her aunt's house because of her cat.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Shortness of breath, coughing, wheezing.
• Constitutional: Fatigue.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops or rubs.
Respiratory: Diminished lung sounds throughout with occasional expiratory wheeze bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pulmonary function test obtained today is consistent with asthma.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Asthma.
• Moderate intermittent asthma.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient’s symptoms are consistent with moderate intermittent asthma based on her history and pulmonary function test results today.
• Patient Education: We discussed the importance of being consistent with inhaled steroid inhaler use as this will help prevent daily symptoms and reduce the need for rescue inhaler use. We also discussed how long acting inhalers like Flovent are not fast acting like albuterol but are important for long term control of asthma symptoms.
• Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Flovent one hundred ten micrograms one puff twice per day to be used consistently as this will help prevent daily symptoms and reduce the need for rescue inhaler use. She can continue using Ventolin inhaler as needed every 4-6 hours p.r.n. We will also work on an asthma action plan together so we know what to do based on her symptoms.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Chronic lumbar back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Larry Garcia is a pleasant 41-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of chronic lumbar back pain. The onset of his pain began after he was moving furniture one weekend. He denies any history of trauma or falls. His pain is described as sharp and stabbing in nature and radiates down to his right leg, all the way down to his toe. He also reports that he has difficulty getting comfortable, which is worse when he sits down. The patient reports that he experiences numbness and tingling in his right leg that radiates down to his foot. He denies any loss of sensation in the genital or rectal area. The patient also denies any weakness or loss of control of his bladder or bowels.

The patient has tried physical therapy before, but this was only temporary relief. He has also been prescribed strong pain medications, but these were only temporary relief as well. The patient has even been recommended surgery in the past, but he would like to avoid surgery at this time.

The patient reports that he used to play golf but this has been difficult due to his back pain.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Chronic lumbar back pain.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient quit smoking 20 years ago.

FAMILY HISTORY

Denies any family history of spine conditions.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Musculoskeletal: Midline tenderness at L4-L5 disk space with right-sided lumbar paravertebral tenderness.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
MRI of the lumbar spine reveals disc herniation with nerve impingement.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic lumbar back pain.
Based on your symptoms, exam, and reviewing your MRI results, your symptoms are consistent with an L4-L5 herniated disk with radiculopathy. This means that one of your disks that sits between your spinal vertebrae is bulging out and this bulge is pinching on some nerves and that’s why you feel that tingling in your leg.
I am recommending a spinal injection with a strong inflammatory medication called a corticosteroid today. We will inject the corticosteroid into your lumbar spine under fluoroscopy which you can think of as an x-ray to help localize to the exact area of your pain. This should help the inflammation that is causing the pain.
The procedure should be relatively quick and common and you should be out of the office within an hour after it’s completed. We will monitor you and see how you respond to this injection and we will schedule another injection if needed at a later date.

Right knee pain.

Kenneth King is a 44-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. He denies hearing anything pop or feeling anything pop at the time of injury. He was able to get out of the water by himself but it was very sore to climb up and any kind of squatting or bending is really pretty sore. He has had no previous history of knee injuries.

The patient reports that he is a frequent water skier and that he tries to go every weekend when they can. He denies any numbness or tingling in his foot.

The patient reports that he has been taking Aleve twice a day for pain relief, as well as applying a cold pack to his right knee.

History of hypertension.
History of tonsillectomy.

Lisinopril 20 mg once a day.
Aleve 2 tablets twice daily as needed for pain.

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain, swelling, and tenderness to palpation.

Neck: No lymphadenopathy appreciated.

note.assessment_and_plan:

Right knee pain:

- Order an x-ray of the right knee today to rule out any fractures which I do not think we will need at this time but we will follow up with you after reviewing those results today.
- Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain and swelling management today as well as health maintenance purposes today due to your history of hypertension.
- Refer you to physical therapy for strengthening exercises around your knee today as well due to your history of hypertension today as well as your current symptoms today.
Medical Reasoning: This particular injury typically heals quite well without surgery but we want to rule out any fractures at this time before proceeding with conservative treatment options such as physical therapy today due to your history of hypertension today as well as your current symptoms today.
Hypertension:
- Continue lisinopril 20 mg once daily per prescription today due to health maintenance purposes today given your history of hypertension today as well as current symptoms today.
- Order lipid panel today due to health maintenance purposes today given your history of hypertension today as well as current symptoms today.
Pain Management:
The patient has been taking Aleve twice daily for pain relief, however I advised him that he should rest his right knee until we have reviewed the x-rays from his examination this morning in order to avoid further injury from skiing again tomorrow.

Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

He states that he has noticed something is always stuck in his throat and that it has been bothering him. He notes that it is more with solid foods, but not liquids. He denies coughing with this issue, but does state that he has thought about potentially choking. He denies blood in his stools or vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
Respiratory: Denies coughing up blood or hemoptysis.
Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Neurological: Denial of numbness or weakness.
note.objective_exam:

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of difficulty swallowing. His examination today was unremarkable except for epigastric tenderness to palpation without evidence of any masses or significant swelling. I am concerned that he may have a stricture causing his symptoms and recommend referral to gastroenterology for endoscopy and dilation if needed.

Regarding his diabetes, we discussed diet and exercise modifications last time. His hemoglobin A1c was 7.4 last time we saw him which was improved at our last visit. We discussed the importance of monitoring his blood sugars at home as well as adjusting his diet to improve glycemic control. I recommended that we repeat his hemoglobin A1c today to see if there has been any improvement since our last visit.

Regarding his hypertension, we discussed lifestyle modifications including weight loss and increased physical activity which he has been following diligently since our last visit. His blood pressure today was 120/50 mm Hg which is within normal limits for office BP but higher than what we had seen previously when he was compliant with lifestyle modifications.

Patient Agreements:
Patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Right ankle pain and instability.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right ankle pain and instability. The patient reports that he was playing basketball with his son Sean when he landed awkwardly and rolled his ankle. He notes that the right ankle is bruised and swollen. The patient reports that he has been having trouble walking due to instability in the right ankle. He recently got back into working out and had been in a good rhythm going to the gym, but he does not want to disrupt that momentum. The patient also reports that he plans to coach his son’s basketball team in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and instability.
Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.
Works from home and plans to coach his son’s basketball team in 04/2022.
Enjoys working out and recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right ankle reveals ecchymosis, swelling, tenderness over the lateral aspect of the ankle, tenderness over the medial deltoid region, no epidermolysis, intact skin, brisk capillary refill.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays were obtained today. These reveal a displaced lateral malleolus at Weber C level. There is no evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lateral malleolar fracture of the right ankle.
Medical Reasoning: This is an unstable fracture due to its location on the lateral side of the ankle.
Medical Treatment: I have discussed this with the patient today. We have discussed his desire to continue coaching starting in April. I have recommended surgical intervention for this fracture which will include placing a plate and screws into his right ankle. We discussed that this will result in approximately 3 months of non-weight bearing status for recovery time. We also discussed that we will provide crutches for him during this time period as well as prescribe meloxicam for pain management until we can get him back into physical therapy again.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with these recommendations.

Evaluation of facial pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Anthony Miller is a 54-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of facial pain. The patient reports that he has had right-sided facial pain for approximately 2-3 months. The pain is described as stabbing and shooting in nature, localized to the right cheekbone area. He notes that the pain is sometimes hot and that it can last anywhere from a few minutes to an hour. The patient denies any sensory loss, numbness, or tingling in the right cheek. He also denies left-sided facial pain. He denies any weakness on that side of the face when smiling or doing other things. The patient reports headaches but denies any history of migraines.

The patient has tried ibuprofen and motrin but these have not helped his symptoms. He has also tried rubbing tiger balm on his face but this did not help either.

The patient notes that certain temperatures seem to trigger his symptoms, as well as cold weather. He denies any history of multiple sclerosis or brain tumors.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Reports no history of multiple sclerosis or brain tumors.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports smoking 1 pack per day for over.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Neurological: Denies vision changes or weakness in right eye.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies left-sided facial pain, sensory loss, numbness, or tingling in the right cheek; Denies right-sided facial weakness; Teeth are symmetric.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neurological: Normal cranial nerves II-XII examination bilaterally. No ptosis, diplopia, ptosis, dysphagia, dysarthria, dysphonia, ataxia or cerebellar signs.
• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the face reveals decreased sensation on the right side compared to the left.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
MRI of the head reveals small blood vessel abutting and perhaps even pinching the trigeminal nerve.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mr Miller is a 54-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of facial pain.
• Medical Reasoning: MRI of the head revealed small blood vessel abutting and perhaps even pinching the trigeminal nerve which may be causing his symptoms consistent with trigeminal neuralgia.
• Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed tegretol (carbamazepine) to start with and we will follow up in one month to reassess his symptoms.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Neck pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brandon Green is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of neck pain. The patient was involved in 4 motor vehicle accidents. He was fine after the first two accidents. The third motor vehicle accident is when his neck and back pain began. He was in therapy following the second accident. He had surgery after his third accident. He was seen at a pain clinic secondary to neck and back pain.

The patient reports that he has been experiencing neck pain since February of this year, which is when he was coming home from the pain clinic because his neck hurts and his back hurts. The patient denies any numbness or dizziness, but does report some headaches and occasional visual disturbances. He endorses sharp, incapacitating pain that prevents him from working.

The patient reports that he has been on fentanyl recently but has not received a prescription for several weeks.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Musculoskeletal: Neck pain, stiffness, bruising, swelling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Pain on palpation both on the bony process and on the muscle.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the neck were obtained today and reviewed in office today. No fractures were identified.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brandon Green is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of neck pain.

I have reviewed his x-rays today and there are no fractures identified. I have discussed this with him today and we have discussed conservative treatment options as well as additional testing options.
I have recommended that we obtain an MRI of the cervical spine to evaluate for any soft tissue injuries.
We will start with Robaxin 1500 mg every 6-8 hours to help with muscle relaxation and reduce tension in this area.
We will also recommend ice application whenever bruising or swelling is present in order to reduce inflammation.
We will also recommend physical therapy to help with range of motion exercises for his neck.
If these symptoms do not improve we can refer him to pain medicine for additional treatment options including local injections.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Carolyn Garcia is a 49-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of her chronic problems. She reports that her osteoarthritis has been flaring up a little bit lately, primarily in her right elbow. She has been sitting at the computer, at the desk more in the office and does not know if it is being stagnant in that position all day which has increased flare-ups for that. She also reports that she has been typing all day versus writing, so it flares up in both elbows. She denies any other joint pain. She does report numbness and tingling in her hands when she is typing for long periods of time, but tries to shake out her arms to relieve that sensation.

Regarding gout, she reports that she had some inflammation of her toe last episode was about 3 months ago. She had some swelling and pain with the toe and states that the medication prescribed by me really controlled it and she has not seen a flare-up since.

Regarding psoriasis, she states that it has been under control too. That has not been a major problem for her either.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Osteoarthritis, gout, psoriasis.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Colchicine 0.6 mg twice a day as needed for gout flare-ups; Steroid cream for scalp psoriasis.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the extremities reveals edema and inflammation of the right olecranon with tenderness and effusion. Pain to palpation of the olecranon bursa and pain with pronation and supination. Pain with flexion and extension of the right arm.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Autoimmune panel was reviewed today by Dr. Dragon. The results were unremarkable without evidence of systemic arthritis or systemic inflammatory process going on.
Uric acid level was reviewed today by Dr. Dragon which was elevated.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Carolyn Garcia is a 49-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of her chronic problems.
- Gout: Everything is nice and stable.
- Osteoarthritis: Right elbow edema, inflammation, tenderness, effusion with pain to palpation of the olecranon bursa and pain with pronation and supination when flexion or extension of the right arm.
- Psoriasis: Stable.
- Medical Reasoning: The elevated uric acid level warrants further investigation into possible gout flare-ups or other etiologies such as hyperparathyroidism or pseudogout.
- Medical Treatment Plan:
 - Continue colchicine 0.6 mg twice a day as needed for flare-ups of gout.
 - Order right elbow x-ray today to evaluate for possible osteoarthritis.
 - Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain and swelling associated with osteoarthritis until x-rays are reviewed by Dr. Dragon.
 - Continue steroid cream for scalp psoriasis.

note.assessment_and_plan:

Donna Lee is a 40-year-old female who presents today for back pain. She was at a surprise party and when the person came in, she jumped out and fell down the stairs. She states that she hit her back into the railing of the staircase. She denies any pain shooting down her legs. The patient reports that her pain is more on the right side of her back. She notes that her pain is worse when she lies flat and any twisting motion makes it worse.

The patient had an injury to her lower back when she was twisting at a birthday party today, but there is no evidence of radiculopathy or nerve compression on exam today. Her MRI from 2 years ago revealed a fusion at T4, which appears to be normal otherwise.

Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Motrin 800mg three times daily with food for pain management today.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.assessment_and_plan:

Michelle Lee is a 31-year-old female with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension who presents with abnormal lab findings today.

Newly diagnosed Lyme disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's positive Lyme titer from last time we saw her combined with her recent insect bite while hiking in the woods supports this diagnosis.
- Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 3 weeks today for treatment of Lyme disease. We will follow up with an infectious disease specialist to ensure there are no additional steps needed at this time. We will schedule another appointment next week for further evaluation of this issue.
- Patient Education/ Counseling Plan: I have counseled the patient on the importance of completing all prescribed antibiotics as directed to ensure full resolution of symptoms and prevent complications such as post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS).
- Patient Agreements/Consent Plan: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Yearly asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Emily Hernandez is a 20-year-old female who presents today for a yearly follow-up for asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergies. Due to insurance changes since her last office visit in April 2020, she was switched from Symbicort to Wixela. She also uses Zyrtec in the spring, summer and fall for her seasonal allergy symptoms which tend to work well. She also has known peanut allergy and tolerates almonds and cashews. Her Asthma Control Test (ACT) score is 21.

The patient reports that she has been doing well overall. She notes that she has not had any urgent care or ER visits for breathing over the past year. She does not believe that she has been put on prednisone for breathing issues.

Regarding her military career, the patient hopes to enlist early spring of 2022. She notes that she has been trying to reduce smoking and vaping in preparation for joining the military. She reports that she rarely uses her albuterol inhaler at this point only before strenuous activity such as going on a run or working out.

She notes that she has been trying to use her daily inhaler less as of late as she is preparing for joining the military. She reports that she usually takes it once in the morning and once at night but occasionally takes it twice a day before strenuous activity.

The patient reports that she is currently using Wixela Inhub 250 mcg-50 mcg/dose powder for inhalation.

Regarding her allergies, the patient states that she typically uses Zyrtec in the spring, summer and fall but more so during springtime. She does tend to use it more just as needed during the summer months when she works outside about three days per week.

She recalls having an experience with peanuts at Enterprise Rent-a-Car where there were many peanuts in one of their cars which gave her hives when touching them. Since then, she has become more cautious around peanuts but still avoids them completely.

The patient reports that she currently keeps an EpiPen with her at all times.

Nose: No nasal polyps or congestion.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Return visit for IBS with functional abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant 32-year-old female who was last seen in August of 2019 with flares of abdominal pain, who was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) that was treated with Bentyl. She had a previous prescription for Reglan that she received from the emergency room that she used as needed for nausea. She was instructed to start a low dose fiber supplement, such as Citrucel, daily, probiotics to help with gas and bloating, Bentyl up to four times daily for intestinal cramping, and stop Reglan and use Zofran as needed. Neuromodulators such as Elavil and Buspar were discussed but not started.

Brittany Edwards reports that she has been going out to eat some on Friday nights and Saturday nights and that she has had some spicy foods or shrimp. She notes that her gut probably does not always appreciate that. She has been experiencing both lower belly cramps and upper belly nausea. She notes that her bowel movements have increased from 2-3 times per day to more than 3 times per day since starting the new diet. She notes that her diarrhea tends to occur after eating pasta or grilled chicken alfredo sauce. She also notes that she tends to have more diarrhea when drinking alcohol.

She reports that she has been avoiding heavy foods due to abdominal pain but notes that she did have some fried chicken today which did not cause any issues.

She reports no tenderness in her abdomen but states it is soft and non-tender without any masses or organomegaly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Gastrointestinal: Positive for diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Abdomen: Soft without tenderness.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant female with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and functional abdominal pain aggravated by high stress, poor eating habits, and poor sleeping habits.

I have encouraged dietary and lifestyle modifications as well as starting a neuromodulator such as Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for IBS.
She can use Bentyl 20 mg as needed 30-45 minutes prior to eating out at a restaurant. She can also use Zofran if needed. However, I have encouraged her to reduce greasy and fatty foods and alcohol consumption.
We discussed long-term medication options including Elavil which would take the place of Bentyl or Zofran when symptoms are present all the time. The only drawback is it can make her sleepy.
She can follow up in one month by emailing over mychart regarding any side effects or issues with elavil or if adjustments are needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Followup for hypertension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Amanda Taylor is a 72-year-old female who presents for follow-up of hypertension. She reports that she has been drinking alcohol 4 to 5 days per week to excess. She denies tobacco use and substance abuse. Her skin is moist, good trigger. On exam she is alert, pleasant, in no acute distress.

She reports that her blood pressure was 130/90 on her last visit on April 16th. After presenting at 150/100, she was prescribed hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg by mouth once daily and lisinopril 20 mg by mouth once daily. CMP and CBC were essentially unremarkable.

The patient reports that she has been taking her lisinopril at half the prescribed dose due to lethargy and headaches in the left ear. She states that she feels much better since taking the half dose and feels like it is helping with her blood pressure.

She denies chest tightness or pressure or shortness of breath with hydrochlorothiazide.

The patient reports that she has been checking her blood pressure at home and notes that in the morning she sees lower numbers than in the evening, where she runs anywhere from like 130 to 145 or 150 over 95 to 100 on the bottom. However, if she sits there for a while and then takes it, it goes down. In the evenings if she sits there for a while and then takes it, it goes down. In the mornings it is generally more normal where it is supposed to be.

She also notes that she takes her medicine in the morning when she gets up instead of in the evening.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Unlabored breathing, cardiac rhythm regular, no murmurs, gallops or jvp elevation.

Alcohol use disorder.
- We discussed naltrexone which we have previously discussed today. She would like to start naltrexone which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today which we have previously discussed today.
- The potential benefit of alcohol cessation would be highly beneficial to her for many reasons including hypertension.
- Her target BP is 130-140 over 70-80.
- We reviewed side effects and risks including nausea, headache, dizziness, anxiety, tiredness and trouble sleeping but generally these are mild and should go away within a few days.
- We will schedule her back week of June 14th when likely around the time of her second naltrexone injection.
- I recommend upgrading influenza vaccination and shingrix.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Thomas Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. The patient reports that his right knee was injected with a steroid injection on 03/04/2021. Since then, he has been experiencing swelling in his right knee and leg. He rates his pain as a 3 out of 10, but typically it is around 6. The swelling has been present for approximately two months. Prior to the injection, the swelling was only in the right knee. The patient states that he has been taking his medications regularly and that Celebrex has been helpful up until the swelling started again.

The patient reports that he has slowed down a little bit and finds some things too fast due to pain. He also mentions that when it really hurts, he has to try and get up from sitting for a while and it is difficult due to stiffness. He notes that after a little while, it loosens up but the first getting up is real difficult.

The patient denies any difficulty with ambulation or activities of daily living.

The patient reports that he wears compression socks frequently but they have not helped with the swelling.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of rheumatoid arthritis.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily; Celebrex 200 mg daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals mild effusion, warmth, erythema, and tenderness over the medial joint line.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Fluid aspiration and steroid injection procedure. The risks, benefits, and alternatives were explained. The risks of steroid injection were explained including hypopigmentation, soft tissue atrophy, tendon ruptures, transient hypoglycemia among others. Verbal consent was attained. The right knee was accessed through the lateral approach with 3 milliliters of initially clear fluid then blood tinged fluid. Then the right knee was prepped in a standard fashion. The right knee was injected with 80 milligrams of triamcinolone and one milliliter lidocaine.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Thomas Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: Thomas Nelson is experiencing persistent swelling in his right knee after receiving a steroid injection on 03/04/2021 which may be related to an effusion or bursitis.
- Medical Treatment: We will proceed with another steroid injection today followed by an x-ray to evaluate for effusion or bursitis.
- Patient Education: We discussed alternative treatment options including physical therapy and surgery if needed as well as dietary modifications such as reducing salt intake to help reduce edema.
- Patient Agreements: Patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of perioral dermatitis.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The onset of his pain began several weeks ago and has been intermittent. He rates the pain as an 8 on a scale of 0 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain he has ever experienced. The patient states that the pain is located in the right upper quadrant, just underneath his ribs. He describes the pain as a squeezing sensation that comes and goes. The patient reports that he gets nauseated and sick in his stomach when he experiences this pain.

The patient reports that his symptoms are related to eating, as they most commonly occur immediately after eating and also a couple of hours later. He denies any fevers or vomiting.

The patient reports that he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes approximately 3 months ago and has been managing it with diet and exercise. He notes that his diet was worse prior to his diagnosis but since then he has cut back on sugar and started a keto diet which has resulted in weight loss of approximately 25 pounds.

The patient denies any family history of gallbladder disease.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient enjoys nature photography.

FAMILY HISTORY

Both parents have had cholecystectomies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Soft non-distended abdomen. Positive for some slight guarding to the right upper quadrant but no rebound tenderness.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
I do believe you have some mild cholecystitis with gallstones. I do not appreciate any frank obstruction but it looks like your gallbladder is inflamed and it looks like that's happened maybe over the last few weeks since you've been having those symptoms.
Since you have not had any improvement with dietary modifications, I am going to make the recommendation that we do remove your gallbladder and I would like to perform a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. This means I'll make a few small incisions and insert a scope with some of those instruments that will remove your gallbladder through one of those little bitty incisions. The surgery will take about an hour to an hour and a half and you'll probably spend the night in the hospital because we just want to monitor you post procedure to make sure everything is okay.
You will still want to avoid those high fat foods after surgery and eat foods that are going to be high in fiber.
Do you have any questions about what our assessment and plan is for this?
The other thing I want to talk briefly about is now your not your type two diabetes, I want you to follow up with your physician just to make sure that you're handling your diabetes especially the fact that you're going to have surgery and those type of things, we will just continue to monitor your diabetes as has been outlined by your endocrinologist or your primary care provider.
The nurse will come in shortly for paperwork signing today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a 67-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right shoulder pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 4 days ago when he was tackled while playing tackle football. He denies any numbness or tingling in his fingers, but reports that his strength is slightly diminished in his right arm. He notes that he has been trying to avoid lifting anything heavy, as reaching down to pick up a box from the driveway was difficult. He denies any neck pain or other orthopedic injuries in the past.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies any numbness or tingling in his fingers.
Cardiovascular: Reports a slight headache.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cervical Spine: No tenderness to palpation of the cervical spine. Full range of motion on head exam. No ecchymosis or bruising.
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of the posterior shoulder at the acromioclavicular joint. Decreased abduction and adduction to about 90 degrees only. Pain with supination and pronation of the right arm. Palpable radial artery pulse.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right shoulder reveals an acute acromioclavicular joint fracture.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

For his right shoulder injury for acute acromioclavicular joint fracture, I have placed him in a sling for now and prescribed meloxicam fifteen milligrams once a day. We will order a CT scan of his right shoulder just to get a better look at how the joint looks and we will refer him to physical therapy to strengthen his shoulder in hopes of avoiding surgery in the future.

Patient Agreements.
Patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jeremy Adams is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of lower back pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 4 months ago when he was moving some boxes when his son was moving out of his college dorm. He states that he felt a “tweak” in his lower back at that time and has been experiencing low back pain ever since. He denies fevers or chills. He also reports right foot tingling, which resolved after about an hour. He denies bowel issues and bladder issues. The patient reports that he is able to support his upper body weight now, but still experiences lower back pain when turning a certain way or rolling over in bed. The patient states that he has been taking Tylenol and ibuprofen for pain, but notes that the ibuprofen seems to be better for a shorter period of time than the Tylenol.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking Tylenol and ibuprofen.

ALLERGIES

The patient reports no known allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No bony protuberance noted.
Lumbar Spine: Decreased flexion and extension of the lower back. Positive straight leg raise test bilaterally. Spasm of paraspinal muscles of the lumbar spine on musculoskeletal exam.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the lumbar spine were obtained today and reviewed by me in office today. There were no acute bony abnormalities noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Jeremy Adams is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of lower back pain.
I do believe it sounds like you have an acute disk herniation based on your history and exam findings today.
I have ordered a lumbar spine MRI to get a better look at what's going on with your spine.
I have also referred you to physical therapy through our health system to help with your symptoms.
I have prescribed meloxicam fifteen milligrams once daily to help with your pain.
We will discuss other treatment options if needed at that time.

Regarding his hypertension, the patient reports that his blood pressure has been running low since this illness began. His home blood pressure is usually around 120/70 mm Hg but sometimes goes as low as.
