note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Scott Miller is a 36-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 3 days ago when he was playing pickup soccer and felt a pop in his right knee. He notes that his right knee is swollen, but the swelling has decreased. He reports that his knee feels limited in motion and that he is unable to bear weight on it or walk on it at all. His gait reveals a marked limp on his right leg.

Examination of the right knee reveals effusion and ecchymosis. There is tenderness to palpation over the medial joint line.
Neurovascularly, bilateral lower extremities are intact.
Muscle strength of 5/5 bilaterally.
Lachman test positive.
Range of motion reveals significant effusion in the right knee with slight ecchymosis, limited terminal extension to about 115 degrees, and limited terminal flexion secondary to pain.
Neurological: Denies any numbness or weakness.

Based on my examination today, Scott Miller's right knee injury is suggestive of an anterior cruciate ligament tear (ACL tear). We will order an MRI today to evaluate for ACL integrity. In the meantime, I have prescribed meloxicam 5 mg daily for anti-inflammatory effects as well as ice if needed for swelling and pain management. We will also need him to wear a knee immobilizer and use crutches while walking around until we get results from MRI results.

Patient Agreements:
The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Teresa Sullivan is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 4 days ago when she was working on pottery. She has been creating pottery for her son's birthday and has been working on a ceramic bowl with full decorations. She reports that she has been doing a lot of work on the bowl and that it is causing her right elbow pain. She states that the pain radiates down her arm and along the medial aspect of her arm. She denies any history of trauma to the elbow, but does report that she has been icing the area for 2 days with no improvement. She reports that she has been taking ibuprofen, but this has not helped with her symptoms.

She also reports that she has a history of hypertension and diabetes type 2. She is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
Endocrine: Reports diabetes type 2.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the extremities is normal bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness over the medial epicondyle of the right elbow.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow was reviewed in clinic today by Dr. Smith, PA-C, who notes no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elbow pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of right elbow pain consistent with medial epicondylitis. This is an overuse injury caused by damage to tendons in her arm.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed conservative treatment options including rest, ice, ibuprofen, and a custom right arm sling to wear while awake. We also discussed how we might consider physical therapy if symptoms persist after 2 weeks.
- Medical Treatment Plan: I have ordered a custom right arm sling for use while awake. I have also prescribed ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours with food for one week to help manage her symptoms. We will follow up in 2 weeks at which time we will discuss additional treatment options if needed.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with this plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that the ulcer has been present for approximately 1 year. She notes that she initially had a little blister on her right foot, which she picked at and it became infected. She then went to her primary care provider (PCP) who prescribed antibiotics, which seemed to help initially. However, the ulcer has not healed and she has been on antibiotics with Keflex for the past 5 months. She denies any trauma to the foot and denies pain.

The patient reports that she is experiencing increased drainage from the ulcer and feels more fatigued lately. She denies fevers or chills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Musculoskeletal: Pain.
• Neurological: Decreased sensation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard.
Respiratory: No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi appreciated.
Cardiovascular: No edema in the lower extremities.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right foot reveals a 1 by 2 centimeter 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. There is minimal granulation tissue present with yellow slough. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection. There is no necrosis present around the wound site. There is no odor present and there is no bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of right foot was performed today and revealed no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.
• Non-healing diabetic foot ulcer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient has been on antibiotics with Keflex for approximately 5 months but her ulcer has not healed. We did an x-ray today which revealed no evidence of osteomyelitis so we can continue with conservative management including debridement in office today followed by colagenase ointment application once daily until we see improvement in wound size. We will also prescribe her a surgical shoe to wear while she continues to walk around at the zoo this weekend as well as continue with regular shoe wear until we see improvement in wound size.
• Medical Treatment: We will order an ABI (ankle brachial index) today to determine blood flow in order to determine if surgical intervention may be necessary at this time. We will also schedule her back in for another office visit in 2 weeks for another debridement if needed at that time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up after an interior STEMI.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Anderson is a 74-year-old female who presents for follow-up after an interior STEMI where she required another stent placement. She reports that she was experiencing similar symptoms to her last heart attack, including chest pain that would not go away. She went to the emergency room and was told that she needed another stent. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. She has been able to exercise at all since her last visit with the exception of walking her dog daily.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes.
Surgical: RCA stent placement in 2018.
SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that she walks her dog daily and enjoys pizza and tries (a type of food).
MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking aspirin 81 mg daily; Brilinta 90 mg twice daily; Lipitor 80 mg daily; Toprol 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; metformin.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: No carotid bruits.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Some lower edema swelling on the right radial artery. The cath site is clean, dry, and intact without hematoma. Palpable right radial artery pulses.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

EKG shows normal sinus rhythm, good R wave progression, evolutionary changes anticipated after STEMI.
Echocardiogram shows reduced ejection fraction of 35%.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Primary diagnosis is coronary artery disease. We will continue aspirin 81 mg daily and Brilinta 90 mg twice daily. We will continue Lipitor at 80 mg daily and Toprol at 50 mg daily. We will refer her to cardiac rehab so we can get some education and give her some confidence to get back to exercising regularly. I think most patients love cardiac rehab and I think you'll do pretty well for this.
Second diagnosis is newly reduced left ventricular dysfunction and moderate mitral regurgitation. I think what that means is that your heart is pumping a bit concerning but I think given your history it will improve over time. We got you into the cath lab pretty quickly so I think the muscle is just kinda stunned like surprised and since you're compliant with your meds I think you will recover. We are going to continue lisinopril at 20 mg daily however considering that you are retaining fluid I think that your third diagnosis is acute heart failure. We are going to prescribe Lasix at 40 mg once a day and Aldactone at 12.5 mg once a day as well as repeat an echo in about two months.
Hypertension seems fine with aldactone but we do want to maybe get you into some nutrition counseling to consider other diet options such as cutting out meat especially any kind of preserved meat like pepperoni but maybe finding you some alternatives.
Patient understands.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling. She reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for approximately 6 months, but they have been more persistent over the last month. She notes that the numbness and tingling are present all the time, while the pain is present when she is typing on her keyboard. She reports that ibuprofen helps with the pain, but resting her right hand also helps. She notes that her mouse also causes pain. The patient denies any nocturnal pain or sleep disruption due to her symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right hand numbness and tingling.
Neurological: Reports right hand pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the upper extremities reveals decreased grip strength in the right hand compared to the left. Tinel's sign is positive over the right wrist.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling.

I have reviewed her chart today and I believe she has carpal tunnel syndrome based on her history and examination findings today. We discussed this with her today as well as treatment options including conservative treatment with a wrist splint at night, ibuprofen up to 600 mg four times daily, and possibly physical therapy if needed. We discussed surgical options as well if conservative treatment fails.

We will start with a wrist splint at night today to help with symptoms. We will also order an EMG/nerve conduction study in her wrist to further evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome.

Patient Agreements Obtained.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

George Young is a 59-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago when he was playing lacrosse with his children. He reports that he was throwing the ball and suddenly started experiencing right elbow pain. He denies any specific mechanism of injury, but believes that his son may have hit him with the lacrosse stick. The patient states that he has been taking ibuprofen for his pain, but notes that he usually forgets to take it. He reports that the pain is sharp and radiates down to his forearm.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he plays lacrosse with his children.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Normal examination of both upper extremities.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right elbow reveals tenderness to palpation over the olecranon process. Mild pain with flexion and extension.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow obtained today was reviewed in office today and is unremarkable without evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

George Young is a 59-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right elbow contusion. I have reviewed his x-ray today which was unremarkable without evidence of fracture or bony abnormality. I have prescribed him 800 mg ibuprofen twice daily for swelling and pain management. Additionally, I have recommended icing his right elbow three times per day for 20 minutes at a time to help reduce swelling and pain as well. We discussed that he should avoid playing lacrosse with his son until further improvement is noted in order to allow healing time. We will follow up in 2 weeks at which point we will review additional labs including an A1c to assess for any changes in diabetes management.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain. The onset of his symptoms began yesterday after he slipped on icy ground while taking out the trash. He states that he was being careful and noticed a little patch of ice. He was able to walk on it initially but today he states that he is limping and has been elevating his right ankle and icing it. He has been taking ibuprofen as needed for pain.

The patient denies any numbness in his foot.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient enjoys playing soccer for the community league.

MEDICATIONS

Ibuprofen: As needed for pain.
note.objective_exam:

Right ankle: Ecchymosis over lateral malleolus associated with swelling. Tenderness to palpation anterolaterally in soft tissue. No laxity on anterior drawer or inversion stress testing. No bony tenderness on palpation of the foot.
Neurovascular: Capillary refill is less than 3 seconds with strong dorsalis pedis pulse. Sensation is intact to light touch.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Right ankle x-ray obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain.
For his right ankle pain, I have reviewed his x-rays today and they are consistent with a right ankle sprain without fracture. I would like him to keep his leg elevated especially when seated and continue icing it as tolerated. He will also be given an Aircast which will help stabilize the ankle and crutches for the next 1-2 days until he may start walking on it as tolerated.
I have advised him that his symptoms should significantly improve in 2 weeks at which time we will reevaluate him at that time.
INSTRUCTIONS
Continue taking NSAIDs as needed for any associated pain.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Cruz is a 17-year-old non-binary immensipated minor with no significant past medical history presents for evaluation of newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia. She reports that she went for her annual checkup and the cholesterol level was elevated. She was told to come in today. She denies any family history of hypercholesterolemia. She does not recall any family history of heart disease or sudden death. Her grandparents reported that her cousin died at age 44 due to a heart attack.

She enjoys being outside and riding her bike on trails, but she does not smoke.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports elevated cholesterol.
Musculoskeletal: Denies any issues with growing up.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood pressure looks good.
NECK: No thyroid gland enlargement.
HEENT: No exophthalmos, no thyromegaly.
NECK: No thyromegaly.
ABDOMEN: No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cholesterol level was elevated at 210.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elevated cholesterol level.
• Medical Reasoning: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that all children be screened once they become between ages 9 and 11 and again between ages 17 and 20. Studies have shown a link between high cholesterol and premature heart attacks. Therefore, we will order a full cholesterol panel today to evaluate for familial hypercholesterolemia or secondary causes of hypercholesterolemia. We will also order a complete metabolic panel, thyroid studies, and liver panels today to evaluate for other causes of hypercholesterolemia. We will also perform genetic testing to see if this problem is familial or secondary in nature.
• Patient Education: I reviewed the results with the patient today and discussed the importance of maintaining a healthy lifestyle including eating a well-balanced diet including foods lower in saturated fat and sugars, as well as continuing to be active and exercise regularly such as biking which she enjoys doing.
• Medical Treatment: We will follow up in 3-6 months after she has met with the nutritionist who can provide information about what kind of foods to eat, instituted dietary changes, and we will repeat her cholesterol level at that time.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Chest pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female today complaining of chest pain. She has a past medical history of diabetes type 2 and high blood pressure. She denies chest pain at this time, but reports that she experiences pressure and dull chest pain when she starts walking. She has been experiencing this for approximately 3 months. She denies any exacerbating or relieving factors. The patient denies shortness of breath, sweating, or clamminess.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
Neurological: Denies chest pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: No jugular venous distention. No carotid bruits.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Cardiac: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Regular rate and rhythm.
Musculoskeletal: No edema in the extremities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female today who presents for evaluation of chest pain.

Chest Pain:
- Stable angina is suspected due to her history of diabetes and the suspected history of high blood pressure as well as her family history of heart disease in the past. We reviewed her EKG today which was normal with no signs of a heart attack. We discussed this with the patient and I have referred her to cardiology for further evaluation today.
- Prescription for aspirin daily, baby aspirin 81 mg once daily, and nitroglycerin prescribed today if she experiences chest pain while walking that does not resolve after taking one or two pills.
- Patient understands.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's EKG was normal but we do not want to rule out unstable angina due to her history of diabetes and high blood pressure as well as her family history of heart disease in the past.

Diabetes:
- The patient is doing fairly well with diet control but she has been having higher blood sugars due to decreased activity levels. We discussed this with the patient and I have recommended that she follow up with ophthalmology for an eye exam in two weeks as well as continue with metformin 500 mg twice daily until we see how things go at our next visit in two weeks when we will order another hemoglobin A1c test.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's hemoglobin A1c was last checked at 7% which is good but not ideal. We discussed dietary modifications with the patient today including reducing soda consumption which she loves, but also increasing physical activity levels which she has been trying to do more recently due to her increased fatigue from higher blood sugars. We also discussed starting her on some dietary modifications that may help with blood pressure control which may also help with weight loss and reduce her risk for diabetes complications such as retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, etc., all while continuing metformin until we see how things go at our next visit in two weeks when we will order another hemoglobin A1c test.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure trended high over the last few years so we are going to start her on hydrochlorothiazide today at a low dose to help control her hypertension as well as reduce some edema that she has been experiencing in her lower extremities. We will monitor these findings closely over the next few weeks by using home monitoring devices and reviewing these findings in clinic each week until we see how things go at our next visit in two weeks when we will review these findings again along with reviewing any additional labs that were ordered today including another hemoglobin A1c test.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sophia Jackson is a 30-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral knee pain. The onset of her pain began approximately 6 months ago and she denies any specific injury. She describes the pain as deep achy behind her kneecaps and hears creaking in her knees. She notes that the pain is worse when getting from a seated position to standing, after watching TV, and going up and down stairs. She reports that resting for some time helps with her pain. She has tried icing, wrapping with an ace bandage, ibuprofen, or Aleve but prefers to avoid taking medications. She does try to be as active as possible but has decreased her mileage from 5-6 miles per day to less than half a mile due to her knee pain.

The patient reports that she has been running for many years but now she can only run half a mile before experiencing knee pain. She enjoys running outdoors but prefers running on a treadmill during the winter months.

She denies any swelling or redness in her knees and has never injured her knees before.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports bilateral knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Normal.
NEURO: Motor strength is 3/5 for abduction of legs bilaterally and remainder of muscle strength for lower extremities are 5/5.
MSK: Examination of gait is normal.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of bilateral knees were obtained today and reviewed by me today. There are no fractures or osteoarthritis noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Based on the patient's history, examination, and review of her x-rays today, I have reviewed this with her in detail today. Her symptoms are consistent with patellofemoral pain syndrome which is a very common condition that we see that causes knee pain especially in active young people. This condition has to do with the way your kneecap which is your patella how that moves along the groove of your thigh your thigh bone which is the femur.
I recommended ibuprofen or anti-inflammatory as needed to help with the pain today. We will also start physical therapy where they will show you a number of lower extremity exercises which will help increase your lower extremity strength, mobility, and correct any incorrect running mechanics that you may have.
We discussed goals for treatment today including getting back into running again but we will need to take it easy from running for now until we assess further progress at our next visit.

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kyle Morales is a 58-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of low back pain. The onset of his pain began approximately 2 weeks ago when he was lifting a box of books. He denies any specific mechanism of injury. The patient reports that his pain is localized to his low back and radiates down his left leg. He describes the pain as achy and sharp. The patient notes that the pain has been getting worse and he has tried ibuprofen and Tylenol, which sometimes help.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling associated with his pain. He also denies any loss of sensation or weakness. He does not report any loss of control of his bladder or bowels.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela Powell is a 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 1 week ago when she was running with her niece and fell, twisting her knee in some kind of funky way. She reports that she heard a pop at the time. She states that she has been limping ever since and it has not gotten better. She rates her pain as a 4 out of 10, which she notes has been getting worse. She reports that she has been taking Tylenol for pain management, but notes that it only lasts for about 2 hours before the pain returns.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: The patient reports that she had an ulcer not too long ago.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is running with her niece.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the left knee reveals edema and effusion. There is moderate range of motion, but not all the way. There is pain on flexion and extension of the knee. Negative Lachman's test and negative valgus/varus test.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the left knee were obtained today and are not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Angela Powell is an 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of left knee pain.
I do believe this to be a medial collateral ligament strain based on her physical exam findings today.
We did obtain x-rays today which were normal, so there are no fractures or bony abnormalities present.
I have prescribed tramadol 50 mg twice daily for pain management as well as Tylenol as needed for breakthrough pain.
I have also placed her in a knee immobilizer to keep her from moving her knee so we can allow it to heal.
She will ice it three or four times per day for twenty minutes at a time to help reduce swelling.
I advised her that I do not want her running with her niece for the next three weeks until we allow time for healing to occur.
She will follow up with me in 2-3 days if she feels like she is getting worse.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Emergency room follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diane Baker is a 28 year old female with a past medical history, significant for depression and hypertension who presents for emergency room follow-up.

The patient reports that she went for a walk yesterday because it was sunny and nice. She felt light-headed and started to fall. She was with her boyfriend at the time and he caught her. They then went to the emergency room.

She reports that her blood pressure was elevated in the emergency room, almost 200. She denies headaches. She has had high blood pressure once a week or once a month, usually when she is traveling for work and not eating as well. She does not bring her blood pressure cuff with her when she travels.

Regarding her depression, she started therapy last year and has been going once a week. Her support system includes her boyfriend, mom, and brother who are all close to her.

She denies chest pain or shortness of breath at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports lightheadedness.
Neurological: Reports headache.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard over the left lower sternal border.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Electrocardiogram stable in comparison to last year.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

High blood pressure: The patient's blood pressure today in the office does look elevated still. We will discuss this further today. Her current lisinopril dose is moderate and we will increase it to 40 mg once daily. We will continue to check her blood pressures through the patient portal and make adjustments if necessary. We may need to add another agent as well.
Depression: The patient's depression appears to be well-managed at this time with therapy once weekly. We discussed this further today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Alan Butler is a 61-year-old male who presents today with complaints of shortness of breath. The onset began over the weekend after he took a very long bike ride, approximately 3 hours. He reports that he was very light-headed and short of breath. He denies chest pain, fever, or any other symptoms. He notes that his vision has been stable since his cataract surgery 4.5 months ago.

Mr. Butler reports that he has been under control with Imitrex for migraines as needed and is currently taking Protonix for reflux.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fevers.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.
• Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports abdominal pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without jugular venous distension.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Respiratory: Auscultation of lungs reveals expiratory wheeze bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pulmonary function test was within normal limits today. Chest x-ray obtained today is normal with no pulmonary edema or pneumonia noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Today, Alan Butler is a 61-year-old male who presents to the clinic today with complaints of shortness of breath. His examination today reveals expiratory wheeze bilaterally on auscultation of the lungs. His pulmonary function test was within normal limits today and his chest x-ray obtained today is normal with no pulmonary edema or pneumonia noted. I have reviewed his prior results and they are all within normal limits.
I have discussed this case with the patient and we have reviewed his prior results in detail today. We have also discussed his current medications in detail as well as his history of migraines and reflux disease. We have reviewed the results from his pulmonary function test and chest x-ray today as well as reviewing the review of symptoms completed by the nurse practitioner prior to our visit today.
At this point in time, I believe that he may have had an asthma exacerbation from exercising and from allergies, however, we will need to follow up with a pulmonologist to confirm this diagnosis. I would like to prescribe him albuterol inhaler for shortness of breath or wheezing as needed for now until we can follow up with a pulmonologist.
Regarding his reflux disease, everything seems stable at this point in time so we will continue on protonix as needed for now until we can follow up with a gastroenterologist to discuss further management options for him.
The patient understands and agrees with these recommendations.

Abnormal lab findings.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joyce Price is a 50-year-old female who presents for follow-up to an abnormal lab finding. She reports that she has been feeling really tired lately over the past couple of months. She used to be very active, running and climbing, but over the past month, she has noticed that her energy has really gone down. She has been so tired and exhausted and has not been able to keep up with her exercise routine. She denies any blood in her stools or dark stools. She denies spotting with her periods. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, body aches or weight loss.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Cardiovascular: Dyspnea on exertion.
• Respiratory: Shortness of breath.
• Gastrointestinal: Constipation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border. No murmurs heard elsewhere.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Tenderness to palpation in right lower quadrant.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c is 8.2; Labs are within normal limits; Anemia labs are pending.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Abnormal lab findings.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's hemoglobin level is low at 8.2 and she should have a hemoglobin level of 13-14 g/dL for her age and gender. We need to investigate why it is low.
• Medical Treatment: We will schedule an endoscopy and colonoscopy just to make sure that she is not bleeding from inside her belly.
• Patient Education/ Counseling: I gave the patient a lot of credit for staying away from french fries and fried chicken, which are high in sodium and can cause fluid retention in patients with congestive heart failure.
• Patient Agreements/Consent: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Logan Harris is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of an upper respiratory infection. The patient reports that about a week ago he started to get a cold. In the last 2-3 days, it seemed to move into his chest. He has had some post nasal drip for the beginning of the week, but it has left his head and gone right down to his upper chest. He denies any fever, shortness of breath, or chest pain. The patient reports that he has been doing well with his diet, but there was some travel over the last week or so which may have impacted this. He is currently taking Crestor 20 mg daily and tolerates it well without any muscle aches.

The patient reports that he had both doses of the COVID-19 vaccine and denies any symptoms related to this.

The patient denies anyone else in his household being sick.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Respiratory: Reports post nasal drip and bilateral ronchi in lungs.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Head and Neck: Cervical lymphadenopathy.
• Respiratory: Bilateral ronchi in lungs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Lipid panel: Within normal limits.
COVID-19 test: Positive.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Logan Harris is a 57-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of an upper respiratory infection. His examination today reveals cervical lymphadenopathy and bilateral ronchi in lungs. His lipid panel was within normal limits. His COVID-19 test was positive.

His upper respiratory infection is likely viral in nature given his positive COVID-19 test and mild symptoms. I have advised him to quarantine for 10 days while avoiding contact with other household members as well as take off work if symptoms worsen. We will follow up with him at that time if needed.
His high cholesterol is currently well controlled on Crestor 20 mg daily. We will continue him on this medication going forward while continuing to watch his diet.
His coronary artery disease seems under control at this time given that he continues to exercise without chest pain. We will order another lipid panel in 6 months as well as perform a stress test in 6 months.

Joint pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

James Moore is a 57-year-old male who presents today with joint pain. The patient reports that he has been putting a few more miles on the bike each day and that his knees have been killing him, just more so in the last 3-4 days. The patient states that it is equally painful in both knees. He notes that it is more painful in the morning when he wakes up, but also notes that by the end of the day, he starts to feel the same sensation, kind of like around dinner time or so. The patient denies any swelling or redness of his knees. He denies any other associated fatigue or fever.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
Musculoskeletal: Reports bilateral knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Auscultation of heart reveals a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, which we have heard in the past. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the knees reveals bilateral edema and slight erythema. There is a slight effusion present on the right knee. Pain to palpation of the right knee. Decreased range of motion bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was obtained today and reviewed by me today. There are no bony abnormalities present and no fractures were identified.
note.assessment_and_plan:

1. Joint pain.
- Medical Reasoning: I am concerned that this may be from a flareup of his lupus.
- Patient Education: I will review this with him today.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an autoimmune panel to further evaluate for this possibility.
2. Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: His EKG was stable compared to last year and his vital signs look good today.
- Patient Education: We discussed this with him today.
- Medical Treatment: We will order a lipid panel and another echocardiogram.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluation of numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of numbness and tingling in his hands. The onset of these symptoms began approximately 3 weeks ago, after he sustained a motor vehicle accident in December 2019 resulting in broken wrists. He states that the numbness and tingling have been progressively worsening over the last month. The patient reports that the right wrist is more affected than the left, but both have gotten worse since his injury. He notes that he wears a splint on his right wrist, but not on his left. The patient also reports mild neck stiffness, which he attributes to a contusion from the motor vehicle accident.

The patient describes the numbness and tingling as occurring on both sides of his hands, starting from the middle and ring finger up to about the elbow. He notes that they are more noticeable at night and throughout the day, but they come and go. The patient denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers.

The patient reports that he has been taking nerve pain medicine prescribed by his primary care provider, but has not been consistent with taking it as prescribed.

The patient denies any history of thyroid issues.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Fatigue, weight gain.
GI: Excessive appetite, bloating.
Eyes: Floaters.
Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath, leg swelling.
Endocrine: Always hungry.
Skin: Dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Gout, muscle pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
- Sensation: Normal pinprick sensation distal to the right wrist. Decreased pinprick sensation in third and fourth fingers on right hand. Decreased sensation in fourth and fifth fingers on left hand.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Today's examination revealed bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome. However, given his symptom presentation today suggests bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome as there is nerve irritation in both wrists secondary to past trauma causing pain and tingling symptoms described by him today.

We will schedule an EMG study today to further evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome. After this study is completed we will discuss treatment options at your next visit including possible injections or surgery referral to our hand clinic if needed. We will also consider an orthopedic referral for additional treatment options if needed.

Patient Agreements obtained.

Kimberly Taylor is a 60-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of bilateral hand numbness and tingling. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 3 months ago, after she sustained a motor vehicle accident where she sustained bilateral wrist fractures. She reports that the numbness and tingling have been progressively worsening over the last month. She notes that the right side is more affected than the left, with numbness and tingling from her middle and ring finger up to her forearm. She also notes some numbness in her pinky on the left side. She denies any pain associated with these symptoms, but does report that they feel weaker when she is using them. She also reports mild neck stiffness, which she attributes to a contusion from hitting her head during the accident.

The patient reports that she has been taking nerve pain medication, but has not been compliant with it.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.
GI: Reports excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Reports floaters.
Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Positive diabetes, always hungry.
Skin: Nail bed trenches, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Gout, muscle pain.
Neurological: Parasthesia, bilateral hands.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological:
- Sensations normal except for diminished pinprick sensation in 3rd and 4th fingers on right side. Diminished pinprick sensation in 4th and 5th fingers on left side.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, question of bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.
- I discussed my impression with the patient today. We discussed conservative treatment options including wearing splints at night as well as during activities that exacerbate symptoms. We also discussed possible surgical intervention if symptoms do not resolve with conservative measures. We will schedule an EMG/NCV to further evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome today.
- If her symptoms do not resolve after EMG/NCV testing we can consider referral to our hand clinic for possible symptomatic injections or carpal tunnel release surgery although she can pursue these through her current orthopedist today as well.
End of note.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney. She reports that she has been experiencing some stomach burning. She endorses hesitancy while urinating and she states she has to wait for her urinary flow to commence. She endorses occasional dysuria. Ashley denies hematuria. Some beverages are associated with dysuria, thus the patient drinks mainly water, Gatorade and V8 juice.

The patient plays on softball team and is interested in joining a drill team over the summer.

Patient reports that her paternal grandfather had myocardial infarction, posterior urethral valves, obstructive neuropathy, end stage chronic kidney disease was dialysis dependent, failed renal transplant.

Patient reports that her paternal great aunt had end stage chronic kidney disease is dialysis dependent, type II diabetes, hypertension.

No family history of polycystic kidney disease.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS: Pepcid 40 mg once daily. Claritin as needed for allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Normal rate and rhythm. No murmurs or gallops heard.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Mild tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound was performed today and revealed an atrophic right kidney. CT abdomen and pelvis was also performed today and revealed cysts on the right kidney and ovaries as well as some lymphadenopathy. CMP was also performed today which revealed elevated creatinine levels.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's abdominal pain may be related to her atrophic right kidney which is causing her left kidney to work harder than normal. This could explain her hesitancy while urinating as well as occasional dysuria associated with certain beverages such as soda.
- Patient Education: We discussed the importance of staying well-hydrated during physical activity such as softball in order to avoid dehydration which can put tremendous strain on the kidneys. We also discussed the importance of maintaining a healthy diet and active lifestyle in order to keep her kidneys healthy as an adult.
- Medical Treatment: We recommended that we perform an annual ultrasound to monitor the size of her kidneys and their overall function, complete a urinalysis to continue to make sure that protein and blood are not in her urine, and do a blood pressure check annually. Additionally, we recommended avoiding non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines like ibuprofen in favor of Tylenol instead.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands all recommendations provided by me today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sean Phillips is a 35-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of left back pain. The onset of his pain began approximately 1 year ago after undergoing lumbar microdiscectomy in 11/2020. He was highly dosed up on gabapentin for severe nerve pain through his back and lower extremities prior to the surgery. He reports that he has had left side low back pain since the surgery. His significant other always tells him to stretch and it always helps, but he has not tried icing or taking any pain medications.

The patient reports that bending over makes his pain worse. He denies any specific physical activities that make his pain better or worse.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left low back pain.
Neurological: Reports no numbness or weakness in the lower extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the lumbar spine reveals tenderness to palpation over the left L5-S1 region without radiation into the left lower extremity.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray images of the lumbar spine reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae. Previous surgical site is visible and appears to have healed properly.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Sean Phillips is a 35-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of left low back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient underwent lumbar microdiscectomy in 11/2020, which resulted in left low back pain. The x-rays reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae, however there is some tenderness to palpation over L5-S1 without radiation into the left lower extremity.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed physical therapy for him as well as meloxicam instead of ibuprofen due to high dose use of ibuprofen. We will follow up with him after physical therapy and if needed we can refer him to a pain management specialist for further evaluation and management.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Emily White is a 77-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The patient reports that she has been experiencing difficulty reading and straight lines, as well as her door frames looking crooked. She also reports that she has been having trouble adjusting to dim lights when dining out at McDonald’s. She denies any history of macular degeneration.

The patient reports that she smokes approximately 1 pack of cigarettes per day.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: The patient reports that she takes her blood pressure when she can remember to do so.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that she smokes approximately 1 pack of cigarettes per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Visual: Reports sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.
• Neurological: Denies any history of macular degeneration.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Ocular: Anterior segment examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. The cornea is clear without media opacities, no microaneurysms, or cataracts. The cup-to-disc ratio is 2 in the right eye and 3 in the left eye. Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina to be attached without any tears or holes or pigment epithelium changes in the fovea. Posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula, thickening of the retina, presence of subretinal fluid and exudates accumulation, positive for hemorrhage. Left eye: Cornea is clear without media opacities, no microaneurysms, or cataracts. No pigment epithelium changes in the fovea.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
Optical coherence tomography shows drusen deposit. Retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation. The choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized. Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
Medical Reasoning: The diagnostic tests and eye exam are really indicative of neovascular age-related macular degeneration which is advanced to a stage that usually leads to more severe vision loss due to abnormal blood vessels growing beneath the retina which will leak fluid and blood creating a large blind spot in the center of visual field which is usually caused by smoking.
Plan: I have discussed this with her today and we have decided to proceed with Lucentis injections once a month after numbing with lidocaine for pain control over a period time which may slow rate of vision decline or stop further vision loss but however disease progression may also occur despite treatment.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Price is a 28-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began after she fell off her mountain bike while mountain biking. She reports that she heard a pop in her right ankle at the time of the injury. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes. She notes that she has been mountain biking for 3 years and does not remember where she usually goes mountain biking. She denies taking anything for pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain.
Neurological: Reports numbness in her heart.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Temperature: 98.6; Blood Pressure: 118/77; Heart Rate: 77 bpm.
MSK: Examination of the right ankle reveals edema and erythema on the lateral malleolus on the right hand side, associated ecchymosis, and a few excoriations. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral malleolus. There is decreased flexion and extension of the right ankle as well as internal and external rotation. There is no apparent injury to the knee or foot.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was obtained today and reviewed by me today. The radiographic findings reveal no acute fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for evaluation of right ankle pain secondary to an acute sprain. I have reviewed her x-rays today which reveal no acute fracture or bony abnormality, just some soft tissue injury.
I have placed her in an air cast with crutches today and prescribed meloxicam fifteen milligrams once a day to help with pain management. We will ice the area for about twenty minutes five times a day as tolerated, weight bear as tolerated, and we will follow up in 2 weeks if she does not improve.

- Right elbow pain is consistent with musculoskeletal etiology given his lack of history of trauma or injury to the right arm. We will obtain an EKG today to evaluate for possible ischemia or myocardial infarction.
- Hypertension is well controlled with Norvasc 2.5 mg daily; however, we will obtain a home blood pressure monitor today to allow him to monitor his blood pressure at home.
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus is well controlled with Metformin 500 mg daily; however, we will obtain a glucose test today to evaluate for glycemic control and adjust medication as needed.
- Chest pain is consistent with musculoskeletal etiology given his lack of history of trauma or injury to the chest area; however, we are concerned for possible cardiac etiology as well. We will obtain an EKG today to evaluate for possible ischemia or myocardial infarction.

We have also discussed this possibility with the patient's brother who is a cardiologist who also believes that this could be cardiac in origin based on his recent hospitalization due to constipation which could have caused anxiety leading to angina-like symptoms. We have discussed these findings with the patient and he understands that we need to rule out cardiac etiology before ruling out musculoskeletal etiology due to his recent history of hypertension and chest pain.
- Patient Education: I have explained all findings and recommendations in detail today and answered any questions he may have had regarding these findings and recommendations.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hacking cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Hannah Wilson is a 41-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of a hacking cough. The onset of her symptoms began 3 days ago when she was around her sister who had similar symptoms. She has been drinking lots of water and taking over-the-counter cough medication, but this has not helped. She denies fever, shortness of breath, body aches, nausea or vomiting.

She reports that she has had seasonal allergies around spring time and she denies any nasal congestion or sore throat.

She is currently taking metformin 500 mg daily and hydrochlorothiazide daily. Her blood pressure has been elevated at home as well.

The patient reports that she was on vacation last week and started feeling poorly after returning home. She denies diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, weight loss, weight gain.
• Respiratory: Reports hacking cough with green phlegm, sore throat, nasal congestion.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea or vomiting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Head and Neck: Erythema of the pharynx. No exudates in the tonsils. Anterior cervical adenopathy.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cough.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of a hacking cough which started 3 days ago when she was around her sister who had similar symptoms. She has been drinking lots of water and taking over-the-counter cough medication, but this has not helped. She denies fever, shortness of breath, body aches, nausea or vomiting.
- Patient Education: I explained to the patient that most likely this is a viral upper respiratory infection which is causing her symptoms especially being around someone else who had similar symptoms and seems like most likely they spread it to her. I advised her to continue with rest and drinking lots of fluids which will help with her symptoms as well as trying another over-the-counter cough medicine if needed.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed trying Coricidin HBP for the cough today as well as increasing her hydrochlorothiazide to 25 mg once daily in the morning due to increased urination associated with it at home as well as continuing to check her blood pressure several times per day at home to monitor for any further elevation in blood pressure.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Rogers is a 50-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder pain. The onset of her pain began 3 weeks ago and she denies any associated trauma. She is very active and has been renovating her basement recently. She denies any previous history of left shoulder pain. She reports that she has been taking Tylenol Extra Strength, 2 tablets every 6 to 8 hours, which does help with her pain.

The patient reports that she experiences constant left shoulder pain. She notes that she cannot sleep on her left side due to the pain and that it is difficult for her to raise her arm over her head. She notes that without Tylenol, her pain level is a 7/10 but with Tylenol it goes down to a 2/10.

She denies numbness or tingling in her left arm or hand.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the left arm or hand.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Motor strength is intact to light touch bilaterally. Sensation is intact to light touch bilaterally.
Neurovascular: Cap refill is brisk in less than 3 seconds bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray imaging of the left shoulder was obtained today and reviewed by me. There are no signs of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

For your first problem of left shoulder pain, your symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy. This means that the tendons of the muscles of your left shoulder have been injured and the injury happened to the tendons that make up or attach to the shoulder muscles.
I have reviewed your x-ray today and there are no signs of fracture or bony abnormality so we will proceed with an MRI of your shoulder just to make sure nothing else is going on with your left shoulder.
I have also referred you for physical therapy for approximately 6-8 weeks.
You should continue taking Tylenol PRN if your symptoms do not improve we can then consider a steroid injection into your left shoulder which could hopefully get you some relief.
We will start with a conservative approach and see how you do.
INSTRUCTIONS
The patient will follow up with me in approximately 2 weeks.

Michael Anderson is a 22-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left-sided back pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago and has been intermittent. He describes the pain as sharp, but it has also been dull at times. The patient denies any radiation of his pain to his extremities. note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

High blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Theresa Rodriguez is a 41-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of high blood pressure. She has been experiencing headaches for about a month, which are throbbing in nature and are relieved with Tylenol. She also reports dizziness and blurry vision. She denies chest pain or shortness of breath with her headaches. She has been taking her medication as prescribed, but she has been forgetting to take it regularly.

She also reports that she has had diabetes for a long time and is currently taking metformin. She states that she takes her metformin every other day.

The patient reports that she loves McDonald's and eats it all the time, but she does not follow a low sodium diet.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: High blood pressure.
Medications: Chlorthalidone; Metformin.
Allergies: None reported.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: No jugular venous distention on exam. No carotid bruits heard.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Blood pressure was elevated this morning at 172/98 mm Hg.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ms. Rodriguez is experiencing uncontrolled hypertension today. Most of the time, this is multifactorial including diet, medication regimen, and lifestyle factors. We will need to change her current medication regimen today as well as make dietary changes to help reduce sodium intake in her diet.

I have recommended that we continue her current medication regimen today and encourage that she take it daily. We will set up a reminder on her phone to help ensure that she takes it daily. We will monitor her blood pressure at home three times per week to see if there is any improvement with the new medication regimen.
We will also schedule an appointment with a nutritionist to discuss dietary changes to help reduce sodium intake in her diet.
Regarding her diabetes, I have recommended that we increase her metformin dosage to 1500 mg daily. We will continue monitoring her blood sugars as usual to ensure the new medication is effective.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Steven Reed is a 60-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of back pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 2 years ago after he fell and bumped his back while playing basketball. He denies smoking currently, but reports that his 4th cousin has scoliosis. He has gained approximately 80 pounds in the past year. He reports that he has been sedentary and does not engage in any physical activity.

The patient rates his pain and describes it as sharp and throbbing. The pain radiates down his left leg, specifically to his toes, and occasionally causes numbness. He denies any loss of sensation in the genital or rectal area. He does report some weakness, especially when standing for prolonged periods of time. The patient notes that lying on his side provides some relief from the pain.

The patient denies urinary or fecal incontinence.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Reports history of smoking but denies current use.
Surgical: Reports history of scoliosis in 4th cousin.
Family: Reports family history of scoliosis.
Social: Reports weight gain due to lack of physical activity.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking white pills for pain management.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Decreased sensation to light touch at the right lateral thigh at L4 dermatome, patella, and Achilles reflexes are symmetrical.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
MRI of the lumbar spine reveals evidence of disc desiccation and a disc bulge with a paracentral disc herniation resulting in moderate right neural foraminal stenosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Based on your symptoms, exam, and reviewing your MRI today, I have reviewed your case with you today and we discussed treatment options today. We discussed a spinal injection with a strong anti-inflammatory medication called a corticosteroid which should help with inflammation directly targeting the bulge to help you out. We also discussed that if this is unsuccessful we can explore additional options including pain medication or surgery.
We will proceed with a spinal injection today under fluoroscopy guided by an anesthesiologist. We will monitor your response to this injection after it is administered today. If you continue to experience pain after this injection we can discuss additional options including pain medication or surgery.
INSTRUCTIONS
Please schedule your procedure at the front desk.

Right knee contusion.

Joe Reed is a 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began over the weekend on Saturday. He was skiing with some friends and was going down in the snow when he could not see as the two paths came together. The front end of his skis dug into the snow and he ended up doing a cartwheel but stopped halfway through. He could feel a pop in his right knee and then immediately experienced pain in his right knee. He denies any previous knee injuries.

The patient reports that he has been able to walk a little bit, but notes that his right knee is swollen and painful.

The patient reports that he has been icing his right knee and taking Advil for pain management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any numbness or weakness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood Pressure: 110/74 mmHg.; Heart Rate: 64 beats per minute.; Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths per minute.; Oxygen Saturation: 98%; Body Temperature: 97.9 degrees F.
NECK: No lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly, no bruits, no jugular venous distention.
ENT: No otitis media, no rhinorrhea, no sinus tenderness.
NEUROLOGY: No ataxia, no dysmetria, no dysarthria, normal sensation to light touch in all extremities.
MSK: Examination of the right knee reveals edema and ecchymosis surrounding the joint. Positive pain to palpation bilaterally. Pain with flexion and extension bilaterally. Full range of motion bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the right knee were reviewed today by Dr. Smith who notes there is no fracture appreciated nor any bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joe Reed is a 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee contusion.

Imaging findings were consistent with a contusion of the right knee without evidence of fracture or bony abnormalities.
Medical Reasoning:
The patient sustained an injury while skiing which resulted in swelling and pain in his right knee. There was positive pain to palpation bilaterally with full range of motion bilaterally without any restriction noted at this time. X-rays were reviewed today by Dr. Smith who notes there is no fracture appreciated nor any bony abnormalities.
Medical Treatment:
The patient will need to rest this area apply ice two-three times daily for twenty minutes at a time take nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medication such as ibuprofen every six to eight hours as needed until improvement is noted. If symptoms do not improve we may consider physical therapy as well.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Recent diagnosis of stage three nonsmall cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of her recent diagnosis of stage three nonsmall cell lung cancer. She reports that she has been experiencing shortness of breath over the weekend. She had previously been very active, taking mile-long walks with her doberman. Her husband has been her support system and her daughter has also been helpful. She is currently taking cisplatin, etoposide, and Zofran.

The patient reports that she has been coughing but denies phlegm. She denies fever. She does report pain when swallowing, which she describes as a sharp pain in her chest when swallowing. The patient denies any body aches or sore throat.

On questioning, the patient reports that she was very devastated when she received this diagnosis and is trying to figure everything out. She notes that she is fortunate to have her husband and daughter with her.

The patient reports that she was nauseated and tired after receiving chemotherapy but took Zofran which seemed to help.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath, dry cough, dysphagia.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
• Respiratory: Crackles in bilateral lungs.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Patient presents today for follow-up of stage three nonsmall cell lung cancer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient’s recent chest x-ray shows evidence of left upper lobe nodule measuring 4.4 cm in size. We are currently treating with neo-adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin and etoposide to try to reduce the tumor size prior to surgical resection.
• Medical Treatment: We will continue the current chemotherapy regimen as tolerated. We will also continue radiation therapy at 45 Gy in fractions for a total of 5 weeks due to the radiation pneumonitis we have seen on chest x-ray today. We will prescribe prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days to help reduce inflammation in the lungs and improve breathing.
• Patient Education/ Counseling: I discussed with the patient the importance of staying well hydrated while undergoing cancer treatment due to risk of dehydration from chemotherapy and radiation therapy. I also discussed with her the importance of continuing with physical activity as tolerated during this time period as well as maintaining adequate nutrition through diet or supplements such as Ensure.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.
